text:
Can you write an email to people who didn't renew their farm share? I run a 30-acre vegetable farm and sell 22-week shares that people pick up every Thursday.

Facts:
- Last year 260 households had a share. 97 didn't renew.
- On July 9 a hailstorm destroyed about half our crops. For the next 6 weeks the boxes had about half the usual amount. We didn't offer refunds or credit, and I sent one short email about it.
- A full share is $540 this year, the same as last year.
- This year we've added a second field on higher ground and put up 2 hail nets over our tomatoes and peppers. That cost $31,000.
- Members can now pause up to 2 weeks and get credit for them.
- Sign-up closes March 15. 52 shares are left.

Under 200 words.

Before I draft, a few questions. These readers left after a season where they paid full price for half-full boxes, got no refund, and got one short email. Your answers will decide how the email deals with that.

1. **Do you want to say anything about last year beyond acknowledging it?** For example: an apology for how you handled it, a credit or discount for returning members, or a promise about what you'd do if a disaster cut the boxes again. Whatever you offer, the email has to commit you to it, so I'll only write in what you're willing to stand behind.
2. **What does the second field protect against?** Is it about spreading risk so one storm can't hit everything, or about drainage, or something else? Hail doesn't usually care about elevation, so I want to describe it accurately.
3. **Do you know why the 97 didn't renew?** Survey answers or things people told you would let the email answer their actual reasons, not the ones we guess.
4. **Who signs it, what's the farm's name, and how do people sign up?** I need a link or another sign-up method.
5. **Anything else from this season you'd want them to know?** For example, how the hail-net crops did, or new crops you've added.

1. Yes. I want to say sorry plainly. I didn't write more after the hail because I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but I should have. I can commit to a credit for any week when weather cuts a box by more than a third, and a short email to members every Thursday of the season. I can't promise there won't be crop loss this year. No discount for returning members.

2. I don't know beyond it being on higher ground.

3. 41 of the 97 answered a short survey in the fall. 29 of them said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks.

4. It's from me, Sam Turner, at Greenbank Farm. Sign-up is through the link on our website.

5. The hail nets only cover the tomatoes and peppers, not the greens. Pickup is still Thursdays at the farm stand. I don't have anything on new crops.

I've added a subject line, but it isn't counted in the word total. The email is about 195 words. A few notes:

- **What it says the field does:** It only says you added a second field on higher ground. It doesn't claim the field protects against anything, since you weren't sure.
- **The survey:** It quotes "29 of the 41 who answered" as you gave it. I didn't turn that into a claim that most of the 97 lapsed members feel this way.
- **The credit:** I kept it to exactly what you're committing to: weeks when weather cuts a box by more than a third. It doesn't say a smaller shortfall gets credit.
- **No name in the greeting:** It opens with "Hello," because I don't know if your email tool can fill in names. Swap in a name field if it can.
- **Sign-up link:** It points to the link on your website. You could paste the direct URL in instead.

Subject: I'm sorry about last summer

Hello,

I'm sorry for how I handled last summer. After the July 9 hailstorm, your boxes were about half-full for six weeks, and all you heard from me was one short email. I was working 16-hour days to save what was left, but I should have written more and made it right.

In our fall survey, 29 of the 41 people who answered said they'd come back if we fixed how we handle bad weeks. So here's what's changed:

- If weather cuts a box by more than a third, you get credit for that week.
- I'll send a short email every Thursday of the season.
- You can pause up to two weeks and get credit for them.
- This year we added a second field on higher ground and hail nets over the tomatoes and peppers, a $31,000 investment.

I can't promise there won't be crop loss, and the nets don't cover the greens. But if it happens, you'll hear from me that week.

A full share is still $540, with pickup Thursdays at the farm stand. Sign-up closes March 15, and 52 shares are left. The link is on our website.

Sam Turner
Greenbank Farm
</final_document>
